pages.body:
Why This Book Exists


When you first start following Jesus, you learn about His life. You learn about His birth. You learn about His miracles. You learn about His death. You learn about His resurrection. He is the hero of the story. He is the Savior of the world. He is the one you follow.


But then you open the Old Testament. You read about Joseph. You read about Moses. You read about David. They are heroes too. They are legends. They are giants of the faith. They did amazing things. They led people. They saved nations. They defeated enemies. You might wonder, "How do they connect to Jesus? Are they just old stories? Or do they point to something greater?"


Here is the secret. They are not the real hero. They are shadows. They are echoes. They are patterns. They are previews. They point to the real hero. They point to Jesus. Joseph was rejected by his brothers. Moses was rejected by his people. David was rejected by his family. But they all became deliverers. They all became saviors. And they all point to the ultimate rejected deliverer. They all point to Jesus.


This book is for you. You are new to the faith. You are building your foundation. Over the next 30 days, we are going to look at the lives of Joseph, Moses, and David. We are going to see their stories. We are going to see their parallels. And we are going to see how they reveal your Savior. They are the heroes. But Jesus is the real hero.


The Value You Will Get


By the end of this book, you will not see Joseph, Moses, and David as just old stories. You will see them as previews. You will see them as patterns. You will see them as blueprints. pages.body:
The Promise (OT)
"Now Israel loved Joseph more than any of his other sons, because he had been born to him in his old age; and he made an ornate robe for him." - Genesis 37:3 (Written around 1800 B.C.)


Joseph was the beloved son. His father loved him more than his other sons. He gave him an ornate robe. He gave him a special gift. He gave him a special place. Joseph was the beloved son. He was a hero. And his story is a clue about Jesus.


The Proof (NT)
"This is my Son, whom I love; with him I am well pleased." - Matthew 3:17


Jesus is the beloved Son. He is the Son of the Father. He is the one whom the Father loves. He is the one with whom the Father is well pleased. Joseph was the beloved son. Jesus is the beloved Son. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The hero is Jesus.


Why It Matters For Your New Life
You are new to the faith. You might wonder if you are loved. You might wonder if you are special. You might wonder if you have a place. Remember Joseph. Remember Jesus. Jesus is the beloved Son. And because you are in Him, you are a beloved child. You are loved. You are special. You have a place.


Faith Builder
Write down this truth: "I am a beloved child of God." Say it out loud. Thank God for loving you.


The Prayer
God, thank you for the example of Joseph. Thank you for the beloved son. Thank you for Jesus. Thank you that He is the beloved Son. Thank you that because of Him, I am a beloved child. Help me to know your love. Help me to follow the real hero. Amen.

pages.body:
The Promise (OT)
"He said to them, 'Listen to this dream I had: We were binding sheaves of grain out in the field when suddenly my sheaf rose and stood upright, while your sheaves gathered around mine and bowed down to it.'" - Genesis 37:6-7 (Written around 1800 B.C.)


Joseph was a dreamer. He had dreams. He had visions. He saw the future. He saw his brothers bowing down to him. He saw his family bowing down to him. He was a dreamer. He was a hero. And his story is a clue about Jesus.


The Proof (NT)
"For the Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost." - Luke 19:10


Jesus is the dreamer. He is the one who saw the future. He is the one who saw the nations bowing down to Him. He is the one who came to seek and save. Joseph was a dreamer. Jesus is the dreamer. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The hero is Jesus.


Why It Matters For Your New Life
You are new to the faith. You might have dreams. You might have visions. You might have hopes. Remember Joseph. Remember Jesus. Jesus is the dreamer. He has a dream for your life. He has a vision for your future. He has a hope for your story.


Faith Builder
Think of a dream you have for your life. Write it down. Ask God to help you pursue it. Thank Jesus for having a dream for you.


The Prayer
God, thank you for the example of Joseph. Thank you for the dreamer. Thank you for Jesus. Thank you that He has a dream for my life. Help me to pursue your dream. Help me to follow the real hero. Amen.
pages.title: Day 2: Joseph the Dreamer

pages.body:
The Promise (OT)
"But when his brothers saw that their father loved him more than any of them, they hated him and could not speak a kind word to him." - Genesis 37:4 (Written around 1800 B.C.)


Joseph was rejected. His brothers hated him. They could not speak a kind word to him. They were jealous. They were angry. They rejected him. He was the rejected brother. He was a hero. And his story is a clue about Jesus.


The Proof (NT)
"He came to that which was his own, but his own did not receive him." - John 1:11


Jesus was rejected. He came to his own. He came to his people. But they did not receive him. They rejected him. Joseph was rejected. Jesus was rejected. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The hero is Jesus.


Why It Matters For Your New Life
You are new to the faith. You might have been rejected. You might have been hated. You might have been dismissed. Remember Joseph. Remember Jesus. They were rejected. They were hated. They were dismissed. But they still became deliverers. They still became saviors.


Faith Builder
Think of a time you were rejected. Write it down. Then write down this truth: "Jesus was rejected for me." Thank Him for understanding your pain.


The Prayer
God, thank you for the example of Joseph. Thank you for the rejected brother. Thank you for Jesus. Thank you that He was rejected for me. Heal my wounds. Help me to forgive those who reject me. Help me to follow the real hero. Amen.

Jesus was sold. He was sold by Judas. He was sold for thirty pieces of silver. Joseph was sold. Jesus was sold. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The hero is Jesus.


Why It Matters For Your New Life
You are new to the faith. You might feel like you have been sold out. You might feel like you have been betrayed. You might feel like you have been abandoned. Remember Joseph. Remember Jesus. They were sold. They were betrayed. They were abandoned. But God was with them.


Faith Builder
Think of a time you felt betrayed. Write it down. Then write down this truth: "Jesus was betrayed for me." Thank Him for understanding your pain.


The Prayer
God, thank you for the example of Joseph. Thank you for the sold slave. Thank you for Jesus. Thank you that He was sold for me. Heal my wounds. Help me to forgive those who betray me. Help me to follow the real hero. Amen.

Why It Matters For Your New Life

God, thank you for the example of Joseph. Thank you for the faithful servant. Thank you for Jesus. Thank you that He served me. Help me to serve others. Help me to follow the real hero. Amen.

The Prayer
God, thank you for the example of Joseph. Thank you for the falsely accused. Thank you for Jesus. Thank you that He was falsely accused for me. Heal my wounds. Help me to forgive those who accuse me. Help me to follow the real hero. Amen.

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Promise (OT)
"But when all goes well with you, remember me and show me kindness; mention me to Pharaoh and get me out of this prison." - Genesis 40:14 (Written around 1800 B.C.)


Joseph was forgotten. He helped a fellow prisoner. He interpreted his dream. He asked him to remember him. But the prisoner forgot him. He was forgotten. He was the forgotten prisoner. He was a hero. And his story is a clue about Jesus.


The Proof (NT)
"My God, my God, why have you forsaken me? Why are you so far from saving me, so far from my cries of anguish?" - Psalm 22:1


Jesus was forgotten. He was forsaken. He cried out on the cross. He felt abandoned. He felt alone. Joseph was forgotten. Jesus was forgotten. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The hero is Jesus.


Why It Matters For Your New Life
You are new to the faith. You might feel forgotten. You might feel abandoned. You might feel alone. Remember Joseph. Remember Jesus. They felt forgotten. They felt abandoned. They felt alone. But God did not forget them. God did not abandon them.


Faith Builder
Think of a time you felt forgotten. Write it down. Then write down this truth: "God never forgets me." Thank Him for remembering you.


The Prayer
God, thank you for the example of Joseph. Thank you for the forgotten prisoner. Thank you for Jesus. Thank you that He was forgotten for me. Thank you that you never forget me. Help me to follow the real hero. Amen.

pages.body:

Why It Matters For Your New Life

Think of a question you have about the future. Write it down. Ask God to reveal His plan. Thank Jesus for knowing the future.


The Prayer
God, thank you for the example of Joseph. Thank you for the dream interpreter. Thank you for Jesus. Thank you that He knows the future. Help me to trust your plan. Help me to follow the real hero. Amen.
pages.title: Day 8: Joseph the Dream Interpreter

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Promise (OT)
"Then Pharaoh said to Joseph, 'Since God has made all this known to you, there is no one so discerning and wise as you. "Therefore God exalted him to the highest place and gave him the name that is above every name..." - Philippians 2:9


Jesus was exalted. He was raised up. He was made King. He was given a name above every name. Joseph was exalted. Jesus was exalted. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The hero is Jesus.


Why It Matters For Your New Life

Faith Builder
Write down this truth: "God will exalt me in His timing." Say it out loud. Thank Him for His plan for your life.


The Prayer
God, thank you for the example of Joseph. Thank you for the exalted ruler. Thank you for Jesus. Thank you that He was exalted. Thank you that you will exalt me. Help me to trust your timing. Help me to follow the real hero. Amen.
pages.title: Day 9: Joseph the Exalted Ruler

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Promise (OT)
"But Joseph said to them, 'Do not be afraid. Am I in the place of God? You intended to harm me, but God intended it for good to accomplish what is now being done, the saving of many lives.'" - Genesis 50:19-20 (Written around 1800 B.C.)

The Proof (NT)
"Jesus said, 'Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing.'" - Luke 23:34


Jesus was a forgiver. He forgave his enemies. He forgave them for crucifying him. He forgave them for hurting him. Joseph was a forgiver. Jesus is the forgiver. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The hero is Jesus.


Why It Matters For Your New Life
You are new to the faith. You might need to forgive someone. You might have been hurt. You might have been betrayed. Remember Joseph. Remember Jesus. They forgave. They forgave their enemies. You can forgive too.


Faith Builder
Think of someone you need to forgive. Write their name down. Ask God to help you forgive them, just as Jesus forgave you.


The Prayer
God, thank you for the example of Joseph. Thank you for the forgiver. Thank you for Jesus. Thank you that He forgave me. Help me to forgive others. Help me to follow the real hero. Amen.
pages.title: Day 10: Joseph the Forgiver

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Promise (OT)
"But when she could hide him no longer, she got a papyrus basket for him and coated it with tar and pitch. Then she placed the child in it and put it among the reeds along the bank of the Nile." - Exodus 2:3 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


Moses was a rescued baby. He was born under a death sentence. He was hidden in a basket. He was placed in the river. He was rescued by Pharaoh's daughter. He was the rescued baby. He was a hero. And his story is a clue about Jesus.


The Proof (NT)
"So he got up, took the child and his mother during the night and left for Egypt, where he stayed until the death of Herod." - Matthew 2:14


Jesus was a rescued baby. He was born under a death sentence. He was taken to Egypt. He was rescued from Herod. Moses was a rescued baby. Jesus was a rescued baby. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The hero is Jesus.


Why It Matters For Your New Life
You are new to the faith. You might feel like you were born into a crisis. You might feel like you were born into danger. Remember Moses. Remember Jesus. They were rescued. They were protected. God has a plan for your life.


Faith Builder
Write down this truth: "God rescued me." Say it out loud. Thank Him for rescuing you.


The Prayer
God, thank you for the example of Moses. Thank you for the rescued baby. Thank you for Jesus. Thank you that you rescued me. Help me to trust your plan. Help me to follow the real hero. Amen.
pages.title: Day 11: Moses the Rescued Baby

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Promise (OT)
"So now, go. I am sending you to Pharaoh to bring my people the Israelites out of Egypt." - Exodus 3:10 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


Moses was a called leader. He was called by God. He was called from a burning bush. He was called to lead his people. He was called to deliver them. He was the called leader. He was a hero. And his story is a clue about Jesus.


The Proof (NT)
"Come, follow me," Jesus said, "and I will send you out to fish for people." - Matthew 4:19


Jesus was a called leader. He was called by the Father. He was called to lead his people. He was called to deliver them. Moses was a called leader. Jesus is the called leader. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The hero is Jesus.


Why It Matters For Your New Life
You are new to the faith. You might be called. You might be called by God. You might be called to do something. Remember Moses. Remember Jesus. They were called. They answered. You can answer too.


Faith Builder
Think of a calling you have. Write it down. Ask God to help you answer it. Thank Jesus for calling you.


The Prayer
God, thank you for the example of Moses. Thank you for the called leader. Thank you for Jesus. Thank you that He called me. Help me to answer the call. Help me to follow the real hero. Amen.
pages.title: Day 12: Moses the Called Leader

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Promise (OT)
"But the LORD said to Moses, 'I will bring you out from under the yoke of the Egyptians. I will free you from being slaves to them, and I will redeem you with an outstretched arm and with mighty acts of judgment.'" - Exodus 6:6 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


Moses was a deliverer. He delivered the Israelites. He set them free. He led them out of Egypt. He led them out of slavery. He was the deliverer. He was a hero. And his story is a clue about Jesus.


The Proof (NT)
"It is for freedom that Christ has set us free. Stand firm, then, and do not let yourselves be burdened again by a yoke of slavery." - Galatians 5:1


Jesus was a deliverer. He delivered us. He set us free. He led us out of sin. He led us out of death. Moses was a deliverer. Jesus is the deliverer. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The hero is Jesus.


Why It Matters For Your New Life
You are new to the faith. You might need to be delivered. You might need to be set free. You might need to be led out. Remember Moses. Remember Jesus. They delivered. They set free. They led out. Jesus can deliver you. Jesus can set you free.


Faith Builder
Think of something you need to be set free from. Write it down. Ask Jesus to deliver you. Thank Him for setting you free.


The Prayer
God, thank you for the example of Moses. Thank you for the deliverer. Thank you for Jesus. Thank you that He delivered me. Help me to live in your freedom. Help me to follow the real hero. Amen.
pages.title: Day 13: Moses the Deliverer

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Promise (OT)
"The LORD said to Moses, 'Come up to me on the mountain and stay here, and I will give you the tablets of stone with the law and commandments I have written for their instruction.'" - Exodus 24:12 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


Moses was a lawgiver. He received the law. He received the commandments. He gave them to the people. He was the lawgiver. He was a hero. And his story is a clue about Jesus.


The Proof (NT)
"For the law was given through Moses; grace and truth came through Jesus Christ." - John 1:17


Jesus is the lawgiver. He is the fulfillment of the law. He is the grace. He is the truth. Moses was a lawgiver. Jesus is the lawgiver. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The hero is Jesus.


Why It Matters For Your New Life
You are new to the faith. You might feel burdened by the law. You might feel like you cannot keep the rules. Remember Moses. Remember Jesus. The law was given through Moses. Grace and truth came through Jesus. You are not saved by the law. You are saved by grace.


Faith Builder
Write down this truth: "I am saved by grace, not by the law." Say it out loud. Thank Jesus for His grace.


The Prayer
God, thank you for the example of Moses. Thank you for the lawgiver. Thank you for Jesus. Thank you that grace and truth came through Him. Help me to live in your grace. Help me to follow the real hero. Amen.
pages.title: Day 14: Moses the Lawgiver

pages.body:

Moses was a prophet. He was the greatest prophet. He spoke to God face to face. He spoke for God. He revealed God's will. He was the prophet. He was a hero. And his story is a clue about Jesus.


The Proof (NT)
"For Moses said, 'The Lord your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your own people; you must listen to everything he tells you.'" - Acts 3:22


Jesus is the prophet. He is the greater prophet. He speaks to God face to face. He speaks for God. He reveals God's will. Moses was a prophet. Jesus is the prophet. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The hero is Jesus.


Why It Matters For Your New Life
You are new to the faith. You might need a prophet. You might need a messenger. You might need someone to speak for God. Remember Moses. Remember Jesus. They were prophets. They spoke for God. Jesus speaks for God. Listen to Him.


Faith Builder
Think of a question you have for God. Write it down. Ask Jesus to speak to you. Thank Him for being the prophet.


The Prayer
God, thank you for the example of Moses. Thank you for the prophet. Thank you for Jesus. Thank you that He speaks for you. Help me to listen to Him. Help me to follow the real hero. Amen.
pages.title: Day 15: Moses the Prophet

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Promise (OT)
"Now Moses was tending the flock of Jethro his father-in-law, the priest of Midian, and he led the flock to the far side of the wilderness and came to Horeb, the mountain of God." - Exodus 3:1 (Written around 1400 B.C.)

"I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep." - John 10:11


Jesus is the shepherd. He is the good shepherd. He tends the flock. He leads the sheep. He protects them. He cares for them. He lays down his life. Moses was a shepherd. Jesus is the shepherd. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The hero is Jesus.


Why It Matters For Your New Life

Faith Builder
Write down this truth: "Jesus is my Good Shepherd." Say it out loud. Thank Him for guiding you.

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Promise (OT)
"But Moses sought the favor of the LORD his God. 'LORD,' he said, 'why should your anger burn against your people, whom you brought out of Egypt with great power and a mighty hand?'" - Exodus 32:11 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


Moses was an intercessor. He prayed for the people. He pleaded for them. He stood in the gap. He was the intercessor. He was a hero. And his story is a clue about Jesus.


The Proof (NT)
"Therefore he is able to save completely those who come to God through him, because he always lives to intercede for them." - Hebrews 7:25


Jesus is the intercessor. He prays for us. He pleads for us. He stands in the gap. Moses was an intercessor. Jesus is the intercessor. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The hero is Jesus.


Why It Matters For Your New Life

Faith Builder
Write down this truth: "Jesus is praying for me." Say it out loud. Thank Him for interceding for you.


The Prayer
God, thank you for the example of Moses. Thank you for the intercessor. Thank you for Jesus. Thank you that He prays for me. Help me to trust His intercession. Help me to follow the real hero. Amen.

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Promise (OT)
"Now Moses was a very humble man, more humble than anyone else on the face of the earth." - Numbers 12:3 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


Moses was meek. He was humble. He was not proud. He was not arrogant. He was the meek. He was a hero. And his story is a clue about Jesus.


The Proof (NT)
"Take my yoke upon you and learn from me, for I am gentle and humble in heart, and you will find rest for your souls." - Matthew 11:29


Jesus is meek. He is humble. He is gentle. He is the meek. Moses was meek. Jesus is meek. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The hero is Jesus.

You are new to the faith. You might want to be great. You might want to be important. You might want to be noticed. Remember Moses. Remember Jesus. They were meek. They were humble. God exalts the humble.


Faith Builder
Think of one way you can be humble this week. Write it down. Ask God to help you do it.


The Prayer
God, thank you for the example of Moses. Thank you for the meek. Thank you for Jesus. Thank you that He is humble. Help me to be humble. Help me to follow the real hero. Amen.
pages.title: Day 18: Moses the Meek

The Prayer
God, thank you for the example of Moses. Thank you for the faithful. Thank you for Jesus. Thank you that He is faithful. Help me to be faithful. Help me to follow the real hero. Amen.
pages.title: Day 19: Moses the Faithful

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Promise (OT)
"Then Moses summoned Joshua and said to him in the presence of all Israel, 'Be strong and courageous, for you must go with this people into the land that the LORD swore to their ancestors to give them...'" - Deuteronomy 31:7 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


Moses was a successor. He prepared Joshua. He prepared him to lead. He prepared him to enter the land. He was the successor. He was a hero. And his story is a clue about Jesus.


The Proof (NT)
"But I will send the Advocate to you—the Spirit of truth, who comes from the Father. And when the Advocate comes, he will tell you what I have told him." - John 15:26


Jesus was a successor. He prepared the disciples. He prepared them to lead. He prepared them to enter the world. Moses was a successor. Jesus is the successor. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The hero is Jesus.


Why It Matters For Your New Life
You are new to the faith. You might need to prepare someone. You might need to prepare the next generation. You might need to prepare a successor. Remember Moses. Remember Jesus. They prepared. They empowered. You can prepare too.


Faith Builder
Think of someone you can encourage this week. Write their name down. Ask God to help you encourage them.


The Prayer
God, thank you for the example of Moses. Thank you for the successor. Thank you for Jesus. Thank you that He prepared the disciples. Help me to prepare others. Help me to follow the real hero. Amen.
pages.title: Day 20: Moses the Successor

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Promise (OT)
"But David said to Saul, 'Your servant has been keeping his father's sheep. When a lion or a bear came and carried off a sheep from the flock, I went after it, struck it and rescued the sheep from its mouth...'" - 1 Samuel 17:34-35 (Written around 1000 B.C.)


David was a shepherd boy. He kept his father's sheep. He protected them. He rescued them. He was the shepherd boy. He was a hero. And his story is a clue about Jesus.


The Proof (NT)
"I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep." - John 10:11


Jesus is the shepherd. He is the good shepherd. He keeps his father's sheep. He protects them. He rescues them. He lays down his life. David was a shepherd boy. Jesus is the shepherd. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The hero is Jesus.


Why It Matters For Your New Life
You are new to the faith. You might need a shepherd. You might need a guide. You might


…..
pages.title: Day 21: David the Shepherd Boy

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
Why It Matters For Your New Life
You are new to the faith. You might need a shepherd. You might need a guide. You might need a protector. Remember David. Remember Jesus. They were shepherds. They guided. They protected. Jesus is your Good Shepherd. He knows your name. He knows your voice. He will never leave you.


Faith Builder
Find a quiet place. Sit down. Close your eyes. Imagine Jesus as your shepherd. Imagine Him leading you beside quiet waters. Write down what that feels like.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being my Good Shepherd. Thank you for guiding me. Thank you for protecting me. Help me to follow you. Help me to follow the real hero. Amen.
pages.title: Day 21: David the Shepherd Boy (Continued)

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Promise (OT)
"So Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed him in the presence of his brothers, and from that day on the Spirit of the LORD came powerfully upon David." - 1 Samuel 16:13 (Written around 1000 B.C.)


David was anointed. He was anointed by Samuel. He was chosen by God. He was set apart as king. He was the anointed king. He was a hero. And his story is a clue about Jesus.


The Proof (NT)
"The Spirit of the Lord is on me, because he has anointed me to proclaim good news to the poor..." - Luke 4:18


Jesus was anointed. He was anointed by the Spirit. He was chosen by God. He was set apart as King. David was anointed. Jesus is the anointed. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The hero is Jesus.


Why It Matters For Your New Life
You are new to the faith. You might not feel special. You might not feel chosen. You might not feel set apart. Remember David. Remember Jesus. They were anointed. They were chosen. God has chosen you too.


Faith Builder
Write down this truth: "I am chosen by God." Say it out loud. Thank God for choosing you.


The Prayer
God, thank you for the example of David. Thank you for the anointed king. Thank you for Jesus. Thank you that He was anointed. Thank you that you have chosen me. Help me to live as your chosen child. Help me to follow the real hero. Amen.
pages.title: Day 22: David the Anointed King

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Promise (OT)
"David said to the Philistine, 'You come against me with sword and spear and javelin, but I come against you in the name of the LORD Almighty...'" - 1 Samuel 17:45 (Written around 1000 B.C.)


David was a giant slayer. He faced Goliath. He faced the giant. He faced the fear. He defeated him. He was the giant slayer. He was a hero. And his story is a clue about Jesus.


The Proof (NT)
"And having disarmed the powers and authorities, he made a public spectacle of them, triumphing over them by the cross." - Colossians 2:15


Jesus was a giant slayer. He faced sin. He faced death. He faced the devil. He defeated them. David was a giant slayer. Jesus is the giant slayer. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The hero is Jesus.


Why It Matters For Your New Life
You are new to the faith. You might face a giant. You might face a giant problem. You might face a giant fear. Remember David. Remember Jesus. They defeated the giant. Jesus can defeat your giant too.


Faith Builder
Think of a giant you are facing. Write it down. Ask Jesus to help you defeat it. Thank Him for being the giant slayer.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being the giant slayer. Thank you for defeating sin and death. Help me to face my giants. Help me to trust your power. Help me to follow the real hero. Amen.
pages.title: Day 23: David the Giant Slayer

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Promise (OT)
"But the LORD said to Samuel, 'Do not consider his appearance or his height, for I have rejected him. The LORD does not look at the things people look at. People look at the outward appearance, but the LORD looks at the heart.'" - 1 Samuel 16:7 (Written around 1000 B.C.)


David was rejected. He was rejected by his brothers. They did not believe in him. They did not support him. He was overlooked. He was dismissed. He was the rejected king. He was a hero. And his story is a clue about Jesus.


The Proof (NT)
"He came to that which was his own, but his own did not receive him." - John 1:11


Jesus was rejected. He came to his own. He came to his people. But they did not receive him. They rejected him. David was rejected. Jesus was rejected. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The hero is Jesus.


Why It Matters For Your New Life
You are new to the faith. You might have been rejected. You might have been overlooked. You might have been dismissed. Remember David. Remember Jesus. They were rejected. But God looked at their hearts. God looks at your heart.


Faith Builder
Write down this truth: "God looks at my heart, not my outside." Say it out loud. Thank God for seeing your heart.


The Prayer
God, thank you for the example of David. Thank you for the rejected king. Thank you for Jesus. Thank you that He was rejected for me. Thank you that you look at my heart. Help me to follow the real hero. Amen.
pages.title: Day 24: David the Rejected King

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Promise (OT)
"David, wearing a linen ephod, danced before the LORD with all his might..." - 2 Samuel 6:14 (Written around 1000 B.C.)


David was a worshiper. He danced before the Lord. He sang to the Lord. He praised the Lord. He worshiped with all his might. He was the worshiper. He was a hero. And his story is a clue about Jesus.


The Proof (NT)
"And when they had sung a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives." - Matthew 26:30


Jesus was a worshiper. He sang to the Lord. He praised the Lord. He worshiped with all his heart. David was a worshiper. Jesus is the worshiper. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The hero is Jesus.


Why It Matters For Your New Life
You are new to the faith. You might want to worship. You might want to praise. You might want to dance. Remember David. Remember Jesus. They worshiped. They praised. You can worship too.


Faith Builder
Put on a favorite worship song. Sing along. Dance if you want to. Thank Jesus for being worthy of worship.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for the example of David. Thank you for the worshiper. Thank you for Jesus. Thank you that He worshiped. Help me to worship you. Help me to follow the real hero. Amen.
pages.title: Day 25: David the Worshiper

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Promise (OT)
"Then David said to Nathan, 'I have sinned against the LORD.' Nathan replied, 'The LORD has taken away your sin. You are not going to die.'" - 2 Samuel 12:13 (Written around 1000 B.C.)


David was a sinner. He sinned. He committed adultery. He committed murder. He messed up. He failed. But he repented. He confessed. He was forgiven. He was the sinner. He was a hero. And his story is a clue about Jesus.


The Proof (NT)
"If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just and will forgive us our sins and purify us from all unrighteousness." - 1 John 1:9


Jesus is the forgiver. He forgives sins. He purifies. He cleanses. David was a sinner. Jesus is the forgiver. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The hero is Jesus.


Why It Matters For Your New Life
You are new to the faith. You might have sinned. You might have failed. You might have messed up. Remember David. Remember Jesus. David sinned. But he was forgiven. You can be forgiven too.


Faith Builder
Think of a sin you are struggling with. Write it down. Confess it to God. Thank Jesus for forgiving you.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being the forgiver. Thank you for forgiving my sins. Help me to confess my sins. Help me to receive your forgiveness. Help me to follow the real hero. Amen.
pages.title: Day 26: David the Sinner

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Promise (OT)
"But now your kingdom will not endure; the LORD has sought out a man after his own heart and appointed him ruler of his people..." - 1 Samuel 13:14 (Written around 1000 B.C.)


David was a man after God's heart. He was called a man after God's own heart. He loved God. He followed God. He pursued God. He was the man after God's heart. He was a hero. And his story is a clue about Jesus.


The Proof (NT)
"I will be a Father to him, and he will be my Son." - Hebrews 1:5


Jesus was the Son of God. He was the Son of the Father. He was the one after God's heart. David was a man after God's heart. Jesus is the Son after God's heart. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The hero is Jesus.


Why It Matters For Your New Life
You are new to the faith. You might want to be a person after God's heart. You might want to love God. You might want to follow God. Remember David. Remember Jesus. They were after God's heart. You can be after God's heart too.


Faith Builder
Write down one way you can pursue God this week. Write it down. Ask God to help you do it.


The Prayer
God, thank you for the example of David. Thank you for the man after your heart. Thank you for Jesus. Thank you that He is after your heart. Help me to be after your heart. Help me to follow the real hero. Amen.
pages.title: Day 27: David the Man After God's Heart

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Promise (OT)
"David said, 'My son Solomon is young and inexperienced, and the house to be built for the LORD should be of great magnificence and fame and splendor in the sight of all the nations. Therefore I will make preparations for it.' So David made extensive preparations before his death." - 1 Chronicles 22:5 (Written around 1000 B.C.)


David was a temple preparer. He prepared the temple. He prepared the house for God. He prepared the materials. He prepared the plans. He was the temple preparer. He was a hero. And his story is a clue about Jesus.


The Proof (NT)
"And I saw the Holy City, the new Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God, prepared as a bride beautifully dressed for her husband." - Revelation 21:2


Jesus is the temple preparer. He prepared a temple. He prepared a house. He prepared a city. He prepared a home. David was a temple preparer. Jesus is the temple preparer. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The hero is Jesus.


Why It Matters For Your New Life
You are new to the faith. You might want to prepare something for God. You might want to prepare a house for God. You might want to prepare a temple for God. Remember David. Remember Jesus. They prepared. They built. You can prepare too.


Faith Builder
Think of one way you can prepare your heart for God this week. Write it down. Ask God to help you do it.


The Prayer
God, thank you for the example of David. Thank you for the temple preparer. Thank you for Jesus. Thank you that He prepared a place for me. Help me to prepare my heart for you. Help me to follow the real hero. Amen.
pages.title: Day 28: David the Temple Preparer

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Promise (OT)
"Then the men of Judah came to Hebron and there they anointed David king over the house of Judah." - 2 Samuel 2:4 (Written around 1000 B.C.)


David was a king. He was anointed king. He was made king. He ruled the people. He led the nation. He was the king. He was a hero. And his story is a clue about Jesus.


The Proof (NT)
"For this reason God highly exalted him and gave him the name that is above every name..." - Philippians 2:9


Jesus is the King. He is the King of Kings. He is the Lord of Lords. He is the one who was exalted. He is the one who was given a name above every name. David was a king. Jesus is the King. The pattern is exact. The shadow is precise. The hero is Jesus.


Why It Matters For Your New Life
You are new to the faith. You might need a king. You might need a ruler. You might need a leader. Remember David. Remember Jesus. They were kings. They ruled. They led. Jesus is your King. He is a good King. He is a kind King. He is a King who loves you.


Faith Builder
Write down this truth: "Jesus is my King." Say it out loud. Thank Him for being your King.


The Prayer
Jesus, thank you for being my King. Thank you for ruling me. Thank you for leading me. Help me to follow you. Help me to follow the real hero. Amen.
pages.title: Day 29: David the King

pages.subtitle: 30-Day Guided Journey
pages.body:
The Promise (OT)
"He is the Rock, his works are perfect, and all his ways are just. A faithful God who does no wrong, upright and just is he." - Deuteronomy 32:4 (Written around 1400 B.C.)


Joseph was a hero. Moses was a hero. David was a hero. They were all heroes. They were all legends. They were all shadows. They were all echoes. They were all patterns. And they all pointed to the real hero. That hero is Jesus.


The Proof (NT)
"For the Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost." - Luke 19:10


Jesus is the real hero. He is the one who came to seek. He is the one who came to save. He is the one who came to rescue. He is the fulfillment of Joseph. He is the fulfillment of Moses. He is the fulfillment of David. He is the real hero.


Why It Matters For Your New Life
You are new to the faith. You might need a hero. You might need a rescue. You might need a savior. Remember Joseph. Remember Moses. Remember David. They were heroes. But Jesus is the real hero. He can rescue you. He can save you. He can deliver you.


Faith Builder
Write down one thing you have learned about the real hero over the last 30 days. Thank God for the real hero. Thank Him for Jesus.


The Prayer
God, thank you for Joseph. Thank you for Moses. Thank you for David. Thank you for Jesus. Thank you for the real hero. Help me to trust the hero. Help me to follow the hero. Help me to live in the rescue of the hero. Amen.



END MATTER


The 30-Day Real Hero Challenge
You have journeyed through 30 days of the real hero. Now what? I challenge you to read the Gospel of John. It is 21 chapters. It will show you how Jesus is the fulfillment of every hero. As you read, look for the pattern. Look for the clues. Look for Jesus.


A Note on Faith
The heroes are evidence. They are evidence of a divine plan. But evidence does not save you. The heroes point to a person. The heroes point to Jesus. You can understand the heroes and still miss the real hero. The invitation is for your heart. Jesus said, "Here I am! I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears my voice and opens the door, I will come in." The heroes are on the table. The door is open. It is your choice.


About the Author
Christine A. loves helping new believers build a strong foundation. He believes that faith is not a blind leap. It is a confident step based on evidence. He lives with his family and enjoys hiking and reading.


Coming Next: Old Testament Shadows
If you enjoyed this journey, the next book in the series goes deeper. Old Testament Shadows takes a 30 day look at understanding the Bible figures who point to Christ. It is for the new believer who wants to go further.


Final Call to Action
Scan the QR code below to get the next book in the series. Visit our website to download a free reading plan. Join our community of believers. The journey is not over. The adventure is just beginning.



Cover Design Concept (The New Believer Edition)


A soft, warm cream or light parchment background. A large, glowing scroll sits in the center. On the scroll, three figures are drawn in simple, friendly lines. Joseph in his colorful robe. Moses with his staff. David with his crown. They are all smiling. They are all pointing to a cross in the center. The title THE REAL HERO is in a strong, trustworthy, bold serif font. The subtitle is in a gentle, welcoming sans-serif. The overall feel is warm, inviting, and full of hope.
